scenes.vo: It covers five and a half million square kilometres. It spans nine countries and territories. And almost everything in it can hurt you.
scenes.foot: [[h0|Almost everything in it can hurt you.]]

scenes.vo: Eels that fire eight hundred and sixty volts.
Ants whose sting hurts for a full day. Spiders, snakes, parasites. And a river that boils.
body: An ant whose sting [[c0|hurts for a full day]].
Spiders. Snakes. Parasites. And a [[c1|river that boils]].

scenes.vo: Explorers called it the green hell. Some walked in, and were never seen again. This is the dark side of the Amazon.
The horrors of the Amazon.

scenes.title: Lost
scenes.vo: Chapter one. Lost.
In 1925, the British explorer Percy Fawcett set out from Cuiabá, into the Brazilian jungle, searching for a lost city he called Z.
scenes.note: 1925: the search for [[m0|the lost city of Z]]

scenes.vo: With him were his son Jack, and Jack's friend Raleigh Rimell. Fawcett had insisted that no one should come looking for them if they failed to return. The three men were never seen again.
scenes.dek: Explorer, son and friend [[f0|never seen again]]
body: Colonel Percy Fawcett, his son Jack and Raleigh Rimell disappear in the Brazilian interior.
Fawcett had insisted [[f1|no one should come looking]] for them.

scenes.vo: They came anyway. Dozens of expeditions went looking for them. Some of those searchers never came back. The jungle kept its secret.
scenes.title: Case file: Fawcett
rows: Percy Fawcett, Jack Fawcett, Raleigh Rimell

scenes.title: In the Water
scenes.vo: Chapter two. In the water.
In 2019, scientists described a new species of electric eel. One was measured firing eight hundred and sixty volts. The strongest discharge of any animal ever recorded.
body: A newly described electric eel delivers [[c0|860 volts]].
It is the [[c1|strongest shock of any animal]] on record.

scenes.vo: And piranhas? Their reputation is mostly a myth. Attacks on people are rare, and usually just a bite, often in the dry season, when the water is low.
body: Piranha attacks on people are [[c0|rare]].
Most are a single bite, often [[c1|in the dry season]].

scenes.vo: Then there's the candiru. A tiny catfish, said to swim into the human body. In reality, there's just one disputed medical case, and experiments found it isn't attracted to urine at all.
scenes.title: Myth file: the candiru
rows: A fish that [[r0|swims into the human body]]

scenes.vo: The real giants are harder to joke about. The black caiman can grow to five metres. The largest predator in the Amazon.
body: Up to [[c0|five metres]] long.
The [[c1|largest predator]] in the Amazon.

scenes.vo: And the green anaconda is the heaviest snake on Earth. It doesn't use venom. It squeezes.
body: The [[c0|heaviest snake]] on Earth.
No venom. [[c1|It squeezes]].

scenes.title: Small Killers
scenes.vo: Chapter three. Small killers.
The bullet ant has the most painful sting of any insect, rated at the very top of the Schmidt pain index. The pain can last up to twenty four hours.
scenes.foot: [[h0|The most painful sting]] of any insect.

scenes.vo: For the Sateré-Mawé people, young men wear gloves woven with hundreds of these ants, as a rite of passage into manhood.
The Brazilian wandering spider has one of the most potent venoms of any spider. Thanks to antivenom, deaths today are rare.
body: One of the [[c0|most potent venoms]] of any spider.
Thanks to [[c1|antivenom]], deaths are now rare.

scenes.vo: The human botfly lays its eggs on mosquitoes. When a mosquito bites, the larvae drop onto the skin, and burrow in. They grow there for weeks.

photo.cap: A botfly larva (rabbit botfly, a close relative).

body: Eggs carried by [[c0|mosquitoes]].
The larvae [[c1|burrow into the skin]] and grow for weeks.

scenes.vo: But the deadliest creature in the Amazon is the smallest. Mosquitoes carry malaria, dengue and yellow fever.
scenes.title: Threat file: the mosquito
The Hunter
scenes.vo: Chapter four. The hunter.
The jaguar is the largest cat in the Americas. Most big cats go for the throat. The jaguar bites straight through the skull.
body: The [[c0|largest cat in the Americas]].
Its bite goes [[c1|straight through the skull]].

scenes.title: The Boiling River
scenes.vo: Chapter five. The boiling river.
Deep in the Peruvian Amazon, hundreds of kilometres from any active volcano, there's a river that runs hot enough to kill.
Its water averages about eighty six degrees, and in places gets close to boiling. Animals that fall in are cooked alive.
scenes.foot: Animals that fall in are [[h0|cooked alive]].

scenes.title: Survivors
scenes.vo: Chapter six. Survivors.
On Christmas Eve 1971, a plane flying from Lima to Pucallpa broke apart in a storm over the jungle.
Seventeen year old Juliane Koepcke fell around three kilometres, still strapped to her seat. She survived, and walked through the jungle alone for eleven days, until she found help.
scenes.dek: Girl, 17, falls [[f0|three kilometres]] and walks out of the jungle
body: Juliane Koepcke survives the fall still strapped into her seat.
She walks alone for [[f1|eleven days]] before finding help.

scenes.vo: And in 2023, in the Colombian Amazon, four children survived a plane crash that killed their mother.
They were found alive forty days later. Their knowledge of the forest, which seeds and fruit were safe to eat, kept them alive.
scenes.foot: Their [[h0|knowledge of the forest]] saved them.

scenes.title: The Real Horror
scenes.vo: Chapter seven. The real horror.
But the biggest threat in the Amazon isn't a jaguar, or a spider. It's us. Roughly one sixth of the rainforest has already been destroyed.
Scientists warn that if losses reach around twenty to twenty five percent, parts of the Amazon could pass a tipping point, and start turning into dry savanna.
scenes.pre: At 20 to 25 percent loss: [[q0|a tipping point]].

scenes.vo: There is hope. In the year to July 2026, Brazil's deforestation alerts fell to their lowest level in more than a decade.
scenes.title: Status file: 2026

scenes.vo: So, could you survive one night alone in the Amazon? Tell me in the comments. And subscribe, for the next story.
